The Texas Water Rights Commission has no land use plans, per se, over which it exercises direct statutory functions of planning, management, and regulation. The principal concern of the Texas Water Rights Commission, in the proposed project in the present stage, is to ensure that a rigorous water rights impact analysis is made; and the principal function is to ensure the protection of existing water rights. These water rights do have a strong connection with and a profound socio-economic impact upon present and future land uses. These water rights are managed by the Texas Water Rights Commission by means of a watermaster system of operation which is characterized by considerable care and precision. Special attention is invited to the enclosed copies of Chapters XX, XXI, and XXII of the Texas Water Rights Commission Rules (Revised 1976), governing the administration of the United States' share, under Texas law, of the water resources of the Rio Grande from Fort Quitman, Texas to the Gulf of Mexico. Therefore, as far as the Texas Water Rights Commission is concerned, the Environmental Impact Statement for the proposed project now being prepared should include a careful analysis of the operational impacts of the proposed project on the water rights administration system which is delineated specifically in the cited Chapters XX, XXI, and XXII.
2. It is believed proper at this time to confirm the fact that in telephone call on April 1, 1976, from Mr. Jim Ligner of the International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC), to Mr. Robert M. Whitenton, Interstate Compact Coordinator, Texas Water Rights Commission (TWRC), request was made for Texas Water Rights Commission's concurrence in a series of controlled releases of water from Amistad Reservoir to simulate power generation releases of the proposed project in order to obtain realistic data for the preparation of the required Environmental Impact Statement. It was understood that IBWC planned to install a series of temporary stream gaging stations and to assign observers along the river in order to document the results of the special releases on the river.
